title: Majestic Sacrifice: Promote With a Rook Fork
summary: Use promotion with check to force a rook block or a king retreat that leaves the rook hanging.

nodes.question: How can White turn promotion into a forcing material gain?
nodes.explanation: c8=Q+ checks along the eighth rank and attacks Rd7 diagonally. Black must block on d8 or retreat to g7, allowing a rook capture in either case.

branches.title: Independent defense: block the promotion check
commentary: Begin after ...Rd7. White’s king is on h2, the promotion pawn is on c7 and the other pawn is on g2. Black retains b6/f6/h7.
c8=Q+ is the source promotion. It checks Kh8 across the eighth rank and attacks Rd7 along c8–d7.
Rd8 is one of two legal replies, independently supplied. The rook blocks the check but lands beside the queen.
Qxd8+ captures the blocking rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win, with all four remaining pawns retained. This branch stops before selecting a further king move.

branches.title: Independent defense: retreat and leave the rook attacked
commentary: Test the other legal reply to the source promotion, without assuming the rook must interpose.
c8=Q+ checks Kh8 and simultaneously attacks the rook on d7.
Kg7 is legal and avoids the eighth-rank check. It leaves Rd7 on the queen’s diagonal.
Qxd7+ captures the rook with check along the seventh rank. The complete seven-piece position is an exact White win; the earlier knight-sacrifice story is not inferred from this finish.

exercises.prompt: What two targets does c8=Q create?
exercises.answer: The new queen checks Kh8 along the eighth rank and attacks Rd7 diagonally.
No. Kg7 is legal too. The queen captures the rook on d8 or d7 according to Black’s reply.
